title.title: A group algebra where $ab = 1$ but $ba \ne 1$
title.subtitle: Claim: a torsion-free group $G$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{F}_2[G]$ with $ab = 1 \ne ba$, so $G$ is not sofic

plain: In this group's arithmetic, a has a right inverse b, yet b times a is not one

beats.text: Kaplansky: a one-sided inverse in a group algebra is two-sided. True in characteristic 0
In characteristic $p$ it holds for every sofic group, and no non-sofic group was known
So a counterexample also proves a non-sofic group exists

steps: Reuse the graph-and-cone machine from the zero-divisor result
Arrange the products so unwanted terms cancel in pairs
Cone surgeries keep the group torsion-free

achievement.label: Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture
statement: ab = 1 \Longrightarrow ba = 1 \quad \text{in every group algebra } K[G]
achievement.context: Before: char 0 for all groups (Kaplansky); sofic groups in char $p$ (Elek–Szabó, 2004)
achievement.note: Also refutes Gottschalk's surjunctivity and the Determinant Conjecture
